newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan won't use fiscal measures as stimulus - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan won't use fiscal measures as stimulus - MOF.

text.p: Japan will not use fiscal measures to stimulate its economy, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday.
He told a news conference Japan would not seek export-led growth, and would continue its policy of achieving domestic demand-orientated economic growth.
"Japan will tell the other members of the Group of Seven (G7) nations that it can achieve the official growth target of 1.9 percent for the current fiscal year," Mitsuzuka said.
Finance ministers and central bank governors of the G7 nations meet in Washington on Sunday.
Misuzuka said G7 cooperation on exchange rates to seek currency stability remains intact.
The G7 issued a statement at a meeting in Berlin in February calling for currency stability.
"I don't want to make any comment on specific currency levels, but I would say that currency stability is important and wild fluctuations are not good," he said.
